paragraphs: Overall credibility check result: not passed. For step s1 (static), reaction balance passed, meaning the applied load is balanced by the support reactions. The mesh quality check also passed, with no inverted elements and very few badly shaped ones.

The maximum von Mises stress convergence check did not pass. The peak stress rises with each refinement, from {{s1.conv2.level0}} on the first mesh to {{s1.conv2.level1}} on the second and {{s1.conv2.level2}} on the third. This is not convergence and suggests a stress singularity, such as a sharp corner or point load. The reported maximum von Mises stress of {{s1.vm_max_mpa}} (away from constrained faces) should therefore not be used as a design basis. The result must not be described as converged or reliable.

The maximum displacement convergence check passed. The values are {{s1.conv3.level0}}, {{s1.conv3.level1}} and {{s1.conv3.level2}} across the three meshes, and the maximum displacement is {{s1.u_max_mm}}. This only shows that the global displacement is mesh-insensitive. It does not remove the doubt about the local stress.
No safety factor is given, because the credibility check did not pass. The material yield strength of {{s1.strength_mpa}} is listed for reference only and is not compared with the stress here.

Limitations: the model is linear elastic with small deformation, with no contact, residual stress or surface hardening. Stresses near constrained and loaded faces come from idealized boundary conditions, and the maximum stress evaluation avoided those regions. Stress at sharp corners grows with mesh refinement (theoretical singularity), so it should not be used directly for design.
suggestions: Locate the position of the maximum stress and check whether it is at a sharp corner or point load.
If the feature is a real geometry detail, add a realistic fillet radius there and refine the mesh locally to re-check stress convergence.
If the singularity comes from a point load or point constraint, replace it with a distributed load or contact patch that reflects the real load path.
Re-run the stress convergence study after the changes, and only evaluate strength once the check passes.
Have an engineer review the corner or load-application detail and decide whether hot-spot or other stress-evaluation methods are needed.
